reference.title: Band Incline Hammer Curl
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the data sheet was not read; the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you curl up, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, short squeeze, about 2.5 s down

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen (bands are colour-coded by tension): pick one you can move for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve; step farther from the anchor, or choke up on the band, for more tension.
prescription.tempo: 3-1-1-0 (2.5 s down, pause in the stretch, 1 s up)
prescription.progression: More reps, a slower lowering, a stronger band.

cues.text: Sit back on a bench set to about 55 degrees, back and head supported, feet flat. A rack stands behind the bench with a band looped low round each upright; hold a band end in each hand, arms hanging straight down behind the trunk line, palms facing in (thumbs forward).
Breathe out and curl both hands up, thumbs leading, keeping the upper arms back and still.
Squeeze at the top, where the band is most stretched; palms still facing each other.
Breathe in and lower slowly against the band to straight arms.
Pause with the arms hanging straight behind the trunk line, then curl again.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arms swinging forward to finish the curl
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows back; let the forearms do the moving.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the back off the pad
mistakes.fix: Keep the back and head on the pad.

mistakes.mistake: Turning the palms up (it becomes a regular curl)
mistakes.fix: Keep the thumbs up and palms facing in throughout.
Straighten the arms fully at the bottom.

kinematics.norm: From straight to about 125-135 degrees at the top (clinical opinion)
Neutral (thumbs up) throughout; the hammer grip shifts work to the brachioradialis (Coratella 2023; Marcolin 2018).
Hangs behind the trunk line, as in the incline curl, which stretches the biceps long head (Oliveira 2009).
Looped low round the rack uprights behind the bench, so it resists the whole curl as gravity does with a dumbbell (clinical opinion)
About 1.2 s up and 2.5 s down (clinical opinion)
About 45-60 degrees (Oliveira 2009 tested shoulder positions in dumbbell curls).

Marcolin et al. 2018, differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl (PeerJ 6:e5165; PMC6047503)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session and replace a worn band; a band that snaps can hit the face or eyes.
Anchor the band to something that cannot move or slip (a rack upright, a pull-up bar or under the feet) and make sure it is secure before loading it.
Band tension rises as it stretches, so the load is heaviest at the end of the pull or push; let it return under control rather than snapping back.
Shoulder pain in the stretched start position: raise the back pad (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: raise the back pad toward upright.
regressions: Seated or standing band hammer curl.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bends the elbow from a stretched position (arms behind the trunk), as in the incline curl (Oliveira 2009); the neutral grip lowers biceps activity a little compared with palms up (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Bends the elbow from a stretched position (arms behind the trunk), as in the incline curl (Oliveira 2009); the neutral grip lowers biceps activity a little compared with palms up (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Brachioradialis is strongly involved with the hammer grip (Coratella 2023; Marcolin 2018), and the hand grips the band.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Brachioradialis is strongly involved with the hammer grip (Coratella 2023; Marcolin 2018), and the hand grips the band.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm back and still.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the upper arm back and still.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk on the pad.
